# Lambda MongoDB Driver Pattern — facts

## How it works

- [statement] The reuse boundary is one Lambda execution environment. Because each MongoClient owns its own per-server pool, Lambda scale-out can create separate pools in separate environments; module-scope caching does not set a fleet-wide Atlas connection cap. This is an inference from AWS's environment reuse guidance and MongoDB's per-client pool model. (high confidence) — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-runtime-environment.html · keywords: Lambda MongoDB Driver Pattern · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/troubleshooting/connection-storms.md, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-concurrency.html, https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/aws-lambda-invocations-trigger-mongodb-connection-spikes/329196
- [statement] AWS Lambda Managed Instances can run multiple Node.js requests concurrently in one execution environment, sharing global objects. When using this mode, isolate mutable request state and use a database client pool that supports concurrent operations; the MongoDB Node.js driver documents one MongoClient supporting multiple concurrent requests. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22) — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-managed-instances-nodejs-runtime.html · keywords: Lambda MongoDB Driver Pattern · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools.md
- [statement] MongoDB's current Node.js driver guide says releases earlier than 6.18.0 did not close idle connections when minPoolSize was 0 during inactivity. Verify the driver version before relying on minPoolSize=0 to reclaim idle sockets. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools.md · keywords: Lambda MongoDB Driver Pattern

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use context.callbackWaitsForEmptyEventLoop=false only with callback-style Node.js handlers; MongoDB's Lambda guide says the setting does not apply to async handlers. AWS currently documents callback-based handlers only for Node.js 22 and earlier runtimes. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/manage-connections-aws-lambda.md · keywords: Lambda MongoDB Driver Pattern · also: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/nodejs-context.html

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] AWS Lambda can purge idle connections, so a later invocation cannot assume an idle socket remains usable. MongoDB's Node.js driver exposes maxIdleTimeMS and minPoolSize to control idle pool behavior; tune these with the workload and test invocations after long idle periods. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/best-practices.html · keywords: Lambda MongoDB Driver Pattern · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/manage-connections-aws-lambda.md
- [statement] Lambda can purge idle connections, so reuse does not guarantee an old socket remains usable. AWS warns that reusing a purged idle connection can error; Atlas recommends maxIdleTimeMS=60000 to reduce serverless timeout errors. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/best-practices.html · keywords: Lambda MongoDB Driver Pattern · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/manage-connections-aws-lambda.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] For standard AWS Lambda, create one Node.js MongoClient outside the handler and reuse it across warm invocations handled by the same execution environment. AWS documents execution-environment resource reuse, MongoDB's Atlas guide shows a module-scope client, and the Serverless Framework example implements the same pattern. Google's Atlas tutorial demonstrates the same instance-local pattern for Cloud Functions. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/manage-connections-aws-lambda.md · keywords: Lambda MongoDB Driver Pattern · also: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/best-practices.html, https://www.serverless.com/examples/aws-node-mongodb-atlas, https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/databases/best-practices-and-tutorial-using-google-cloud-functions-mongodb-atlas
- [statement] Each MongoClient maintains pools per server and opens monitoring sockets in addition to application connections. Set pool limits against expected Lambda concurrency and MongoDB topology; maxPoolSize is not a total connection cap for the deployment. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools.md · keywords: Lambda MongoDB Driver Pattern · also: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-concurrency.html, https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/aws-lambda-invocations-trigger-mongodb-connection-spikes/329196
- [statement] Each MongoClient maintains a pool for each server. The current Node.js driver docs list maxPoolSize=100 by default and up to two additional monitoring sockets per server per client, so estimate connection use across both topology and Lambda environments. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools.md · keywords: Lambda MongoDB Driver Pattern · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/troubleshooting/connection-storms.md
